skill.name: golang-naming
skill.description: Review and choose Go names for packages, functions, types, variables, errors, constants, and tests using detailed conventions and examples.
skill.summary: Apply consistent Go naming conventions during implementation, review, and refactoring.
skill.author: samber

security_audit.summary: All 127 static findings are false positives in naming documentation and evaluation fixtures. Backticks format examples, the traversal match occurs in placeholder comments, and the import match is ordinary Go syntax. content.user_title: Improve Go Naming Across Your Codebase
content.value_statement: Inconsistent Go names make APIs and reviews harder to understand. This skill provides focused conventions and examples for choosing clear, consistent names.
actual_capabilities: Suggest package, file, and import alias names while avoiding repeated context.
Review variable names, receiver consistency, boolean prefixes, and acronym casing.
Recommend constructor, getter, setter, format-function, and functional option names.
Explain interface, struct, constant, enum, sentinel error, and error type naming.
Review test function names, table-driven test fields, and subtest descriptions.
Compare naming alternatives with examples and rationale for each recommendation.
limitations: The skill focuses on naming decisions, not general Go implementation or architecture.
It does not include an executable linter or enforce naming rules automatically.
Safe workspace-wide renames require separate language-server tooling and verification.
Some recommendations are opinionated style choices, not Go language requirements.

use_cases.title: Learn Go Naming Conventions
use_cases.description: Compare familiar naming habits with Go conventions for variables, acronyms, constants, and receivers.

use_cases.title: Review Public API Names
use_cases.description: Evaluate package names, constructors, interfaces, options, and errors before publishing a Go library.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Terminology
use_cases.description: Identify inconsistent domain names and prepare naming recommendations that respect established project conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Naming Choice
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare userId and userID in Go. Recommend one and explain acronym casing.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Go Snippet
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the Go snippet below for naming only: [snippet]. Suggest replacements for variables, receivers, and getters. Explain each recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Design Consistent API Names
prompt_templates.prompt: Review public names for [package] with [types and functions]. Recommend constructor, option, interface, and error names. Consider call sites and existing conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Naming Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [packages or files] for inconsistent domain names. Propose a rename plan, identify public API risks, and separate recommendations from required compatibility checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare a cross-package naming change.

output_examples.input: Review the names userSlice, countInt, contextCtx, and userId.
output: Use users instead of userSlice to describe the contents rather than the storage type.
Use count instead of countInt because the type already communicates that it is an integer.
Use ctx instead of contextCtx to follow common Go parameter naming.
Use userID instead of userId to keep the initialism consistently capitalized.

output_examples.input: Choose constructor and error names for an apiclient package with one primary Client type.
output: Prefer New for the primary constructor so the package-qualified name avoids repeating Client.
Use ErrNotFound for a sentinel error and ResponseError for a custom error type.
Under this skill's style, prefix the sentinel message with apiclient to identify its origin.

output_examples.input: Review a TaskState enum whose zero value is TaskStatePending.
output: The skill recommends TaskStateUnknown as an explicit zero-value sentinel.
Keep the TaskState prefix on enum values for clarity.
Check persisted values and API contracts before changing existing numeric assignments.

best_practices: Provide package context and representative call sites when asking for naming recommendations.
Reconcile the skill's preferences with established project conventions and compatibility requirements.
Use language-server renaming and run relevant tests when applying identifier changes.
anti_patterns: Treating every style preference as a compiler requirement or universal Go rule.
Renaming exported identifiers without checking downstream callers and interface contracts.
Using broad text replacement for semantic renames across a workspace.

faq.question: Which tools does this skill support?
faq.answer: The skill declares compatibility with Codex and Claude Code. Its guidance applies to Go projects.

faq.question: What naming areas does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers packages, files, identifiers, constructors, methods, interfaces, constants, enums, errors, and tests.

faq.question: Does it automatically enforce naming rules?
faq.answer: No executable enforcement tool is included. The skill references linters and separate skills for automation.

faq.question: Can it safely rename every reference?
faq.answer: The skill recommends separate gopls tooling for workspace-wide renames. Review public API compatibility and test the resulting changes.

faq.question: Are all recommendations official Go requirements?
faq.answer: No. Some rules are opinionated, including mandatory boolean prefixes and lowercase acronyms in error messages. Apply project conventions and engineering judgment.

faq.question: Can company naming conventions take precedence?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill states that a company skill explicitly superseding its naming guidance takes precedence.
